content.title: About
content.content: Cottonseed oil is extracted from the seeds of the cotton plant (Gossypium spp.). It is a light‑yellow vegetable oil with a neutral taste and aroma. The oil is rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, especially linoleic acid, and is widely used in cooking, food processing, and cosmetics.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottonseed oil is one of the cheapest vegetable oils worldwide.
Cotton seeds contain about 20 % oil, which is obtained by pressing and solvent extraction.
More than 70 % of the world’s cottonseed oil production occurs in the United States.
The oil is commonly used in margarines, mayonnaise, and sauces because of its high oxidative stability when stored properly.
In cosmetics, cottonseed oil is valued for its gentle moisturizing properties and ability to improve product texture.

items.title: Rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids
items.content: Linoleic acid in cottonseed oil supports cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Skin support
items.content: The oil is often used in skin care to improve barrier function and reduce dryness.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with some other vegetable oils, cottonseed oil contains less saturated fatty acids.

items.title: Contains phytosterols
items.content: Phytosterols may help lower blood cholesterol levels.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Cotton seeds are frequently treated with pesticides; choose refined, quality‑checked oil.

items.title: Cotton allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to components of the oil.

items.title: High omega‑6 content
items.content: Excessive intake of omega‑6 fatty acids can disrupt the omega‑3/omega‑6 balance, which is undesirable for health.

items.title: Trans fats from improper processing
items.content: Unrefined or overheated oil can form trans fats, which are harmful to the heart.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Cottonseed oil is suitable for frying, baking, making sauces and marinades. It can replace more expensive oils in recipes. In cosmetics, it is used in hair masks, moisturizing creams, and lotions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the oil in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it refrigerated to prevent oxidation. Discard oil that has a rancid smell.
